title: Sunny and the Sleepy Koala | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka meets a little koala who can't fall asleep, and together they discover the most peaceful lullaby in the whole bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The moon was rising slowly over the gum trees, big and round and soft as a lantern.

Little Sunny the quokka was out for her evening wander, her paws making the tiniest sounds on the quiet bush floor.

She stopped beneath a tall old eucalyptus tree and looked up.

Something small and fluffy was wedged in the fork of a high branch. Something with big round ears and a button nose.

It was a baby koala.

And the baby koala was not asleep. Her eyes were wide open, blinking slowly down at Sunny.

"Hello up there," Sunny called, very softly. "Can't you sleep?"

The little koala shook her head. "The night is too big," she said, in a tiny koala voice. "And too quiet. And too dark."

Sunny understood. Some nights feel that way.

She sat down at the base of the tree, in a little patch of moonlight, and she listened.

The wind moved through the eucalyptus leaves. A long, slow, sighing sound — like the whole bush breathing out.

"Do you hear that?" Sunny whispered. "The trees are singing."

The little koala tilted her head and listened too.

The leaves rustled again. Softer this time. A gentle shushing sound, like someone whispering everything is all right.

"I hear it," the koala said quietly.

Above them, the moon climbed a little higher. Its light spilled down through the branches, painting soft silver shapes across the bark.

A small moth drifted past on silent wings.

Sunny watched it go. The koala watched it too.

"The moon is keeping watch," Sunny said gently. "It stays awake so you don't have to."

The little koala's eyes grew heavy. She pressed her soft grey cheek against the smooth white bark of the branch.

The leaves whispered again. Shhhh. Shhhh. Shhhh.

Sunny stayed very still, listening to the bush breathing all around them both.

Soon the little koala's breathing slowed. In. Out. In. Out. Her small round ears went still.

She was asleep.

Sunny smiled her gentle smile and looked up at the moon.

"Thank you," she whispered to the trees. To the moon. To the soft quiet night.

Then she curled up in her patch of moonlight, closed her eyes, and let the leaves sing her to sleep too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little koala. Goodnight, little one.
